eyebrow: A PRAYER SERIES ON THE ANGER YOU CAN'T COOL DOWN
coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For the Anger
You Keep Swallowing
coverDek: For the snap you didn't mean, the grudge that's been simmering for years, and the rage that scares you a little — five prayers for the fire you can't seem to put out.

points.hook: I didn't mean to raise my voice like that. I just didn't know where else to put it.
paragraphs: I keep replaying the moment my voice got loud over something that didn't deserve it — the dish left in the sink, the comment that wasn't even really about me. The anger wasn't really about the dish; it was every unspoken thing I'd been carrying finally finding a door. Paul never tells me to stop feeling it — he tells me not to let the sun go down still holding it, because what I don't put down by nightfall I wake up still carrying tomorrow.
points.verseText: Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath:

points.hook: I decree: this temper stops with me.
paragraphs: I decree over my bloodline tonight that the short fuse I inherited does not get handed down to the next name after mine! A soft answer turns away wrath, and I choose the soft answer even when the old pattern in me is screaming for the last word. In the name of Jesus I break the cycle of slammed doors and raised voices that taught me anger was the only language strong enough to be heard — it stops here, it stops now, it stops with me!
points.verseText: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

points.hook: Notice what your body does the second they say that thing again.
paragraphs: Notice it — the heat climbing your neck, the jaw locking shut, the hands curling before your mind has even caught up to what you're feeling. That rush isn't a sin; it's wiring doing exactly what it was built to do. What happens in the next three seconds is the part that matters: swift to hear, slow to speak, slower still to let the wrath out, because the fire in your chest was never meant to drive the car.
points.verseText: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

points.hook: Somebody in this church has been angry about the same thing for years and never said it out loud.
paragraphs: Family, somebody reading this is still rehearsing an old offense from this very congregation — a word said in a meeting, a decision made without them, a hurt that calcified into silence instead of ever getting spoken. Anger left alone doesn't evaporate; it rests in the bosom and waits. If that's you, don't let another anniversary of that hurt pass without bringing it into the light, because a fool nurses a grudge but the wise let it go somewhere real.
points.verseText: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.

points.hook: Child, bring Me the anger before it turns into something that eats you.
paragraphs: Child, I see what you've been swallowing so no one else has to deal with it — and I'd rather you bring the whole fire to Me than let it burn quietly in a place I was never allowed to reach. Cease from the anger and let go of the wrath; fretting over it will only do you evil, never good. Hand Me the heat before it hardens into something that outlasts the thing that caused it.
points.verseText: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.

cta.closingLine: If the fire you've been carrying has been scaring you a little, you're not alone — come back tomorrow for the next series.
